extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients (PD/PIs, institutional officials, and research administrators) preparing RPPRs
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and reporting standards for preparing the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) for various NIH award activity codes (career development, fellowship, SBIR/STTR, training, education, multi-project). Covers required content, attachments, and special instructions by award type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include PII or PHI in the RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI) in the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive PII examples: Social Security Number, personal financial information, Alien Registration Number. PHI example: personal medical conditions. Documents containing sensitive PII or PHI must not be included in the RPPR. NIH recipients: see FAQ or contact IC Privacy Coordinator for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe opportunities for training and professional development (B.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe activities such as teaching, clinical care, professional consultation, advisory service, administrative activities, and other training/professional development provided by the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate percent of time spent in each activity and relationship to the recipient's research career development. For programs involving participants, describe training activities (courses, one-on-one mentoring) and professional development (workshops, conferences). Include conference participation not listed under major activities. For training awards, provide a PDF paragraph for each trainee summarizing training/progress (degrees, mentors, project description and progress, career development activities, conference presentations, role in publications, honors/awards). Do not include biosketches of current/former trainees, sensitive PII, actual IDPs, promotional materials, course syllabi, or program brochures unless NOFO specifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of Individual Development Plans (IDPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the organization uses IDPs, and if so, describe how they were used during the reporting period to manage training/career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the actual IDP document. Requirement applies to mentored career development awards to postdocs (K00, K01, K22, K99, etc.), fellowships, training awards and programs where relevant. Not required for AHRQ recipients (where stated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report mentoring activities for awards that require mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards that include mentoring responsibilities (e.g., K05, K24), describe mentoring effort and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate percent of time devoted to mentoring, list individuals mentored during reporting period, frequency and kinds of mentoring, financial and other support provided to mentees, and productivity of the mentoring relationship. For planned mentoring (B.6), describe proposed mentees (backgrounds, interests, professional levels) sufficient to evaluate quality of mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timeline and plans for next reporting period (B.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline for activities planned for the next year and plans to accomplish the project's goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans to apply for subsequent grant support. For transition awards (e.g., K22, K99) report progress in identifying an independent research position. For fellows include coursework and important modifications; provide scientific justification for any changes involving human subjects or vertebrate animals and provide a detailed description under Changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (C.5.c) applicability and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether Data Management and Sharing (DMS) requirements apply and provide required DMS information when applicable (C.5.c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable for competing applications submitted on or after January 25, 2023 for many activity codes. Specific exceptions and applicability vary by award type (e.g., not applicable for K12, KL1, KM1; applicable for certain career, SBIR/STTR, multi-project activity codes). Refer to NIH Grants Policy Statement 8.2.3.1 and NIH Scientific Data Sharing website for details and complete activity code lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (G.2) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the responsible conduct of research (RCR) instruction received or provided during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the five components: Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration, and Frequency. If instruction occurred in a prior budget period, note dates. Discuss activities undertaken to individualize instruction appropriate to career stage. Additional guidance in competing application instructions. For training awards, describe extent of trainee and faculty participation and name faculty contributors to formal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor’s or Sponsor’s Report (G.3) for mentored awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For mentored K awards provide a mentor-signed letter assessing the recipient's progress and performance during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessment of research progress and development toward independence, information on continued commitment of required minimum professional effort (e.g., nine person months/75% for most K), availability of support for candidate’s research project for next budget segment, and mentor contributions to transition for career transition awards (e.g., K22, K99). If multiple mentors required, assemble letters into one PDF. For fellowships, provide a sponsor's signed letter assessing research training progress and dual-degree progress where applicable. For non-mentored K awards select 'Not Applicable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: What was accomplished under goals / Specific aims and milestones (B.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report accomplishments under stated goals, specific aims, and/or milestones for the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe major activities, significant results (major findings, developments, conclusions both positive and negative), key outcomes or achievements. For SBIR/STTR, goals are equivalent to specific aims and/or milestones; include milestones and indicate whether there are revisions/supplements requiring reporting (identify by grant number/title and describe aims/milestones). For multi-project awards report accomplishments of individual projects/cores under their components and overall award accomplishments at the overall level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Revisions/Administrative Supplements reporting (B.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether one or more Revisions/Supplements are associated with the award and require reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, identify the Revision(s) by grant number (e.g., 3R01CA098765-01S1) or title and describe the specific aims and/or milestones for each Revision. Include supplements to promote re-entry or support addition of an individual or discrete project.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR progress report abstracts and commercialization updates (B.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a one-page abstract describing the research plan for the progress report and updated commercialization information where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast-Track and Phase II should include an updated commercialization plan as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report other products and resource sharing (C.5.a and C.5.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify significant products developed (other products) and report resource sharing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SBIR/STTR, commercial technologies are addressed under Impact. For multi-project awards identify other significant products developed under the overall project and report project/core-specific products and resource sharing under the component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on technology transfer and commercialization reporting (E.3, E.3.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ways the project made or is likely to make an impact on commercial technology or public use, and report status of commercialization activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transfer of results/products to government or industry, instances where research led to start-up companies, adoption of new practices. For commercialization activities, report status with options such as Sales, Licensing revenue, 3rd party investment since award start, Sale of company, Sale of technology rights, Company merger, Joint venture, Marketing/Distribution agreements, Manufacturing agreements, R&D agreements, Customer alliances, Other. [60 character limit for text fields where noted.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Report FDA interactions for SBIR/STTR (E.3.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report interactions with the Food and Drug Administration related to the award technology during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: Not applicable; Discussion with FDA not initiated; Discussion with FDA initiated; Approval in Progress (Applied for approval, Review ongoing, In human clinical trials, Other); Approval Granted: Type; Not approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Life Cycle Certifications and Foreign Disclosure (G.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR recipients must submit Life Cycle Certification forms and address updates to Foreign Disclosure forms when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life Cycle Certification forms must be uploaded within Interim and Final RPPR; I-RPPR or F-RPPR will not be accepted unless all completed Life Cycle Certification(s) are received. Updated SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Forms (Required Disclosures of Foreign Affiliations or Relationships to Foreign Countries) must be submitted via the Foreign Disclosure Request for Additional Materials (RAM) in eRA Commons, have all questions addressed, be signed, and submitted as a flattened PDF. See NOT-OD-23-139 and NOT-OD-25-102 and forms directory links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide childcare costs requests for eligible NRSA fellows and trainees (G.1/G.1 for Training)
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA Individual Fellows and certain institutional training awards may request childcare costs and must upload a specified PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows: upload 'Childcare_Cost_Request.pdf' specifying requested amount and number of years requested (see NOT-OD-21-074). Institutional T32 etc: upload 'Childcare_Costs.pdf' specifying number of trainees who used childcare costs (see NOT-OD-25-100). Recipients are not required to submit supporting documentation with each request but must maintain documentation; NIH may request proof at any time. AHRQ recipients should follow AHRQ-specific notices where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: D.1 Who has worked on the project / Participants table instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide or update information for individuals who worked on the project (PD/PI, Fellow, New Sponsor, New Training Faculty, Other Significant Contributors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellowships, provide or update only for the Fellow (considered PD/PI) and any New Sponsor (considered New OSC). For training RPPRs, New Training Faculty are considered new Senior/Key Personnel and must be entered as a participant and marked 'Yes' for Senior/Key. For multi-project awards, specify component(s) on which the individual worked when editing the participant (Ctrl-select multiple components). Before adding a Biographical Sketch Common Form/NIH Biosketch Supplement for a New Sponsor or new Senior/Key, enter them as a participant in the D.1 table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel and New Senior/Key documentation (D.1 & SciENcv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload Biographical Sketch Common Form/NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement and Current and Pending (Other) Support for new Senior/Key Personnel when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit documentation using SciENcv: Science Experts Network Curriculum Vitae. For new training faculty or new sponsors, enter participant, mark as Senior/Key, then upload Biosketch and Current & Pending forms and supplemental documentation per forms instructions and FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in Current and Pending (Other) Support reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report changes in active Current and Pending (Other) Support for key personnel (e.g., fellow) since the last reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, upload updated Current and Pending (Other) Support and Supplemental Documentation for the fellow, listing the project for which the progress report is submitted and the effort to be devoted in the next reporting period. Use SciENcv forms and follow Common Forms FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications arising from trainee support (C.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report trainee publications associated with the training award in Section C.1 if they were accepted/made public during the initial reporting period and resulted from work conducted while the trainee was supported by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter trainee publications into My Bibliography to display in section C.1 of the RPPR electronic interface. PD/PIs may hide trainee papers for which they were not an author from public display in My NCBI. Full citations of publications arising from trainee work should not be duplicated in the trainee paragraph (they are collected in C.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training award program statistics and Table 8/Table 8A
rubrics_metrics.description: For T awards and specified activity codes provide updated information in Table 8 and program statistics for doctoral training in Table 8A where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: T awards: update Table 8 reflecting new appointments and other changes. Activity codes D43 and U2R require program statistics for doctoral training in Table 8A. Do not report trainee support before/after appointment here (report on Table 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form and justification instructions (H.1 and H.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete and upload the required budget form(s) and provide budget justification per instructions for the selected budget format (SF424 R&R or PHS 398 Training Budget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K awards: follow SF 424 (R&R) Career Development Instructions K-300 and base recipient salary/fringe on full-time, 12-month appointment. For training awards: select applicable RPPR budget type (SF424 or PHS 398) and follow competing application instructions (Section G.300 or G.330). Budget justification must include detailed justification for line items that represent significant change from previously recommended levels (e.g., total re-budgeting greater than 25% of total award amount for budget period). Note: if subaward budgets are completed, the system will not calculate budget line item F.5 for the main budget; total consortium costs MUST be computed and entered manually into budget line item F.5 for the main budget. For subawards/consortium, up to 30 subaward budgets may be entered and competing application subaward forms used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward budget attachment rules (H.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for completing detailed subaward/consortium budgets and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To complete a detailed budget for a subaward/consortium, follow the competing application instructions for the Subaward Budget Attachment(s) Form (Section G.310 for R&R or G.340 for PHS 398 training format). Recipient may select up to 30 subaward budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe changes in approach and reasons for change (F.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe changes in approach for the next budget period and reasons for the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include changes in program/training faculty, the role of external advisory committees, significant new training content/procedures/experiences, and indicate how these changes strengthen and realize objectives and goals. For multi-project awards, describe changes at the component level when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report significant changes to human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, select agents (F.3 / multi-project F.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are significant changes to human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents, provide description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete this section only if the use or care of these is not reported under another NIH award. For multi-project awards, if changes exist, check appropriate box, provide description of changes, and report under the relevant component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR: emphasize synergy, collaboration, and integration (7.6.1 B.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project awards provide an overall description that emphasizes synergy, collaboration, and integration of the major activities of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report major goals specific to an individual component under that component. Overall reporting should highlight integration across components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR: overall accomplishments and unmet goals (7.6.1 B.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the overall award describe major activities, significant results (positive and negative), key outcomes, and discuss stated goals not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report accomplishments of individual projects and cores under their respective components. Identify any Revisions associated with the award or specific project/core and specify the component if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR: participant/component specification (D.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding or editing participants for multi-project awards, specify which component(s) the individual worked on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the participant's three-dot ellipsis icon, click Edit, and select component(s) (use Ctrl to select multiple). Instructions apply for new Senior/Key Personnel and New Other Significant Contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR: budgets for components and system-generated summary
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project RPPRs complete the budget for each component and subaward; a summary budget will be system-generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite budget summaries will reflect direct costs for the recipient. Subaward direct and indirect costs are listed as consortium and include all consortium costs. Total consortium costs for the summary budget are automatically calculated by the system and reflect sum of consortium costs (budget line item F.5) for project budgets with the recipient UEI and total direct/indirect costs (line item I) for project budgets with a different UEI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-project RPPRs with complicated structure: follow R&R budget form (H.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-project RPPRs with complicated structures follow competing application instructions Section G.300 – R&R Budget Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload budget justification as item L and include detailed justification for line items/amounts that represent significant change (e.g., total re-budgeting greater than 25% of total award amount for the budget period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and Not Applicable items (various sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many RPPR sections or specific questions may be 'Not Applicable' for particular award types; follow award-specific applicability notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide repeatedly lists sections/questions as 'Not Applicable' for certain award types (e.g., C.2, C.3, C.4, D.2.a/e, E.1–E.3, F.1–F.3, G.11–G.12). Recipients should follow the award-specific list of applicable vs. Not Applicable items in the instructions for their activity code.
